rationale: Fixed direct check for unit-claim-heartbeat-header-gate (obligation claim-heartbeat-header-gate). The check declares one out-of-window pure heartbeat and drives it through both AppendEntries entry paths on otherwise identical, goroutine-free nodes: processRPC applies checkRPCHeader (declared prerequisite alias normal-rejected: rejected true, no state change) and processHeartbeat reaches appendEntries without it. The property is an assertion on the fast-path result event that the guard was applied, i.e. that term, state, leader identity and last contact were left unchanged; identity is the declared op_id. The oracle reads emitted event fields, not tests_passed, so a passing test with guard_applied false is a violated comparison. An in-window control on the normal path shows the difference is attributable to the header window rather than to the request shape. Local construction testing in a copy of the captured module already shows the expected asymmetry (normal path: 'operation not supported with current protocol version', no state change; fast path: term 0 to 5, leader adopted as ghost-leader, last contact refreshed, guard_applied false), but that run is construction knowledge only and this product fixes the bytes and premises for fresh controller execution. The direct invocation of processHeartbeat is not a shortcut around the dispatch: it is the body of the handler installed by SetHeartbeatHandler, and the package's own integration test calls r.processHeartbeat(rpc) from inside a custom heartbeat handler, which is recorded as a semantic adaptation because the net_transport fast path is reachable only over TCP and the sandbox has network disabled. Reachability of an out-of-window peer and the election consequence remain declared uncertainties rather than assumed facts.
